To find ${g}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(({x}^{2}+y){e}^{{y}^{2}}) \\  & ={e}^{{y}^{2}}+2y({x}^{2}+y){e}^{{y}^{2}} \\  & =(1+2{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y){e}^{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(({x}^{2}+y){e}^{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =2x{e}^{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y)+{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =(1+2{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y){e}^{{y}^{2}}+2x{e}^{{y}^{2}} \\  & =(1+2x+2{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y){e}^{{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
